licensees regarding M.G.L. ch. 138 s. 12D (as codified by Chapter 9 of the Acts of 2025) which would
permit the Board to allow licensees permitted to sell only wines and malt beverages pursuant to M.G.L.
ch. 138 s. 12 to trade in said license and be issued a non-transferable all alcoholic beverages license.
The open comment period has now formally closed.

The Board extends the formal comment period for an additional two weeks, to close on Thursday,
December 4, 2025.

In particular, the Board invites comment and/or draft regulatory language regarding the
following:

   ● Whether to impose any minimum amount of time a licensee must hold a wines and malt
       beverages license prior to applying to change the category to all alcoholic beverages;
   ● Whether to in any way restrict or regulate the ability of an upgraded all alcoholic
       beverages to change location within the City of Boston;
   ● Whether to impose any requirement that the holder of a pledged wines and malt
       beverages license notify holder(s) of said pledge prior to submitting an application to
       upgrade said license.

heading: The Board held an informational hearing on October 21, 2025 to receive public feedback from
item_text:
3. The Board held an informational hearing on October 21, 2025 to receive public feedback from
licensees regarding M.G.L. ch. 138 s. 12D (as codified by Chapter 9 of the Acts of 2025) which would
permit the Board to allow licensees permitted to sell only wines and malt beverages pursuant to M.G.L.
ch. 138 s. 12 to trade in said license and be issued a non-transferable all alcoholic beverages license.
The open comment period was extended to December 3, and has now formally closed.

The Board will draft initial regulations for review on January 8, 2026

Draft regulations will address, at a minimum, the following:
   ● Whether to impose any minimum amount of time a licensee must hold a wines and malt
        beverages license prior to applying to change the category to all alcoholic beverages,
        noting that any licensee who has held a wines and malt beverages license since at least
        January 1, 2025 can apply immediately;
   ● Whether to in any way restrict or regulate the ability of an upgraded all alcoholic
        beverages to change location within the City of Boston;
   ● Waiving community process requirements for applicants who have completed a
        community process in connection with an all alcoholic beverages license within two years
        prior to submitting an application to upgrade.

heading: The Board held an informational hearing on October 21, 2025 to receive public feedback from
item_text:
2. The Board held an informational hearing on October 21, 2025 to receive public feedback from
licensees regarding M.G.L. ch. 138 s. 12D (as codified by Chapter 9 of the Acts of 2025) which would
permit the Board to allow licensees permitted to sell only wines and malt beverages pursuant to M.G.L.
ch. 138 s. 12 to trade in said license and be issued a non-transferable all alcoholic beverages license.
Following the close of an open comment period, the Board discussed principles to be included in final
regulations.

Draft regulations to be voted on or amended are as follows:

        Proposed New Rule 1.08(R)

        R. Licensees permitted under Section 12 to sell only wine and malt beverages,
        with or without the addition of cordials/liqueurs, may apply to trade in said license
        and be issued a non-transferable all alcoholic beverages license pursuant to
        Chapter 138, Section 12D and the following regulations:

heading: If approved, the all alcoholic beverages license shall, upon
item_text:
3.      If approved, the all alcoholic beverages license shall, upon
        issuance, be nontransferable to any other person, corporation, or organization
        and shall be clearly marked “nontransferable” on its face.

heading: A licensee whose license has been upgraded pursuant to this
item_text:
5.      A licensee whose license has been upgraded pursuant to this
        section may apply at any time to “downgrade” to a license to sell only wine and
        malt beverages, with or without the addition of cordials/liqueurs, by submitting a
        “Change of Category” application and required accompanying documentation to
        the Licensing Board. The application is subject to all provisions of Chapter 138,
        including notice, publication, certified mailing, and a hearing. If approved, the
        license shall revert to its category prior to upgrading. If the original wine and malt

      beverages license was a general quota license, the downgraded license shall be
      transferable upon issuance.
